title: Incident signal fusion and targeted replay for config-induced quality drops
creator: Avery Patel
description:
Background:
A recent customer-facing incident showed a sharp drop in answer quality for a small subset of requests after a config rollout (KV cache TTL + batching policy tweak). Current eval/alerting surfaced the symptom (rise in regression metric) but failed to quickly attribute to the config delta or produce a minimal repro that could be used in a postmortem and automated smoke test.

Goal:
Build a repeatable workflow that fuses signals from production traces, eval snapshots, and config-change metadata to:
1) Automatically attribute quality deltas to the most likely config/model change candidate,
2) Generate targeted replay jobs (minimal input set + deterministic runtime flags) that reproduce the quality drop locally and in CI,
3) Auto-create gated smoke-evals from successful replays to prevent regressions in subsequent rollouts.

Scope (MVP):
- Producer: signal fusion microservice that ingests eval alerts, request traces (sampled), and config-change events, emitting ranked candidate causes.
- Replayer: a harness that can run a small, prioritized input slice against specified model/config combinations (hosted and dedicated variants) and capture token-level diffs + eval metrics.
- Integration: CLI/automation that converts a high-confidence candidate + repro to a CI smoke-eval PR template and attaches artifacts to the incident.
- Dashboards: minimal attribution view (candidate list with confidence, example requests, diff metrics) in the Console incident panel.

Non-goals:
- Full causal proof or formal model debugging (out of scope for MVP).
- Automatic rollback/rollforward automation (we will surface options but not auto-execute).

Acceptance criteria:
- Given an eval-alert, the signal fusion service produces a ranked list of candidate config/model changes within 30 minutes, with >= 1 actionable example request when confidence >= 0.6.
- The replay harness reproduces the observed eval delta (>= 90% of metric change) for at least 70% of high-confidence cases in internal test runs.
- A generated smoke-eval PR (template) is created in the customer's rollout repo with repro artifacts and a suggested guard (block deploy on regressions).
- Documentation: runbook + operator guide added to Confluence with example incidents and how to triage fused signals.

Implementation tasks:
- Design signal schema and storage for fused events (traces, eval snapshots, config diffs) (Rohit)
- Implement fusion ruleset pipeline (probabilistic attribution heuristics + feature store) (2 devs)
- Build replay harness: deterministic runtime runner that can accept a small input set + model/config spec and emit token-diff artifacts (1 dev)
- Add integration that constructs smoke-eval PRs and attaches to incident cards (1 dev)
- Console changes: add a compact attribution panel + link to repro artifacts (frontend) (1 FE)
- Create CI job template for smoke-eval execution and pass/fail gating (DevOps)
- Add e2e tests that exercise a known synthetic regression (QA)

Metrics to monitor:
- Mean time to attribution (alert -> candidate list)
- Fraction of alerts with a high-confidence candidate (>0.6)
- Replay success rate (reproducer reproduces metric delta)
- Time from alert to smoke-eval PR creation

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: noisy traces or sparse sampling can reduce attribution confidence. Mitigation: require a minimum number of sampled requests and fall back to best-effort heuristics; surface uncertainty clearly.
- Risk: replayer nondeterminism across hosting modes. Mitigation: capture environment metadata and pin runtime flags; for Dedicated/private, require a compatible image/snapshot.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha: run on a backlog of 12 recent incidents and measure attribution/replay rates (2 weeks).
2) Beta: enable for platform-team alerts with opt-in (4 weeks).
3) GA: enable automatically for all eval-alerts and attach smoke-eval PRs for releases (after validation).

Docs & runbooks:
- Confluence: "Incident signal fusion — operator guide" (link below)
- Runbook steps: triage, run fusion, kick replay, evaluate artifacts, create smoke-eval PR, suggested mitigations.

Notes:
- We should collaborate with Research to prioritize evaluation metrics that are sensitive to config-level changes (KV TTL, batching thresholds, quantization toggles).
- Tie into the existing eval artifact storage (s3://redwood-evals/repro-artifacts) to avoid duplicating payloads.

comments: 2025-02-13 - Triage: Confirmed drop corresponds to config rollout 2025-02-11 (kv_ttl=60->10, batching_policy=v2). Sampled traces show token-level divergence concentrated on long-prefix prompts. - Avery

2025-02-15 - Design sync: Agreed to prioritize signal fusion heuristics that consider time-windowed rollouts and model-compatibility matrices. Need product input on acceptable confidence thresholds. - Rohit
2025-02-17 - Prototype: Basic replay harness can reproduce the delta for 3/5 synthetic cases when we pin seed+runtime flags. Next: capture more env metadata and stabilize CI runner. - Eng
2025-02-20 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness/pull/128 (initial runner + artifact schema). Requesting review from @lisa and @omar. - Rohit

2025-02-24 - QA: Ran alpha against 12 incidents. Fusion produced a high-confidence candidate in 9/12 cases; replay fully reproduced metric delta in 6/9. Action: tune heuristics and improve input prioritization. - QA Team

2025-02-25 - Product feedback: Add an option to mark some repros as 'sensitive' and redact PII before attaching to PRs. Also request an explainability field for why a candidate was ranked. - Priya (PM)
